newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling loses vs dollar on panic buying.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling loses vs dollar on panic buying.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling took a battering from the dollar on Monday in very nervous trading, commercial bank dealers said.
They said they were maintaining wide spreads of around one shilling -- 55.50/56.50 -- unsure of the shilling's direction.
"The market is very jittery today. No-one wants to be caught offguard. Dollars are being picked at any price," one dealer said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean commercial rate of 55.35 against the dollar compared to 55.22 on Monday. On the pound, it was posted at a commercial mean of 89.90 from 89.69.
But with dollars expected later in the afternoon from coffee and tea exporters, some dealers said the market could stabilise.
"Today will be a good test on whether there really is demand or people are just playing up rates," one dealer said.

The shilling's losses have been spurred by increased dollar demand, mainly from industrial importers and companies seeking funds to pay out dividends to offshore investors. But panic dollar buying has triggered a wave of exaggerrated movements, dealers said.
"The central bank has really stayed out of the market. I guess what's happening is good for the market because the shilling is trying to find its true levels," one dealer said.
The money market eased on Tuesday on an inflow of about 3.8 billion shillings from last week's treasury bill auction.
Overnight rates were quoted at between 13 and 20 percent compared to 21 percent on Monday.
